transcript.text: Can you describe your experience leading a drill squad of 30 cadets as Senior Under Officer?

I'm a final-year mechanical engineering student in Dehradun. I hold the NCC 'C' certificate with grade B, and as Senior Under Officer I led a drill squad of 30 cadets. My final-year project is a low-cost solar water heater prototype that reached 55 degrees Celsius in four hours. I also spent three weeks at an auto-components plant. I want an MBA because I found that production decisions are as much about people and cost as machines.
What challenges did you face managing the squad and how did you overcome them?
transcript.anchor_quote: as Senior Under Officer I led a drill squad of 30 cadets

transcript.text: NCC has taught me discipline, leadership and national integration. I believe in leading from the front and I will bring the same spirit to my MBA and to my career.
Can you share a specific example of a challenge you encountered while leading the drill squad, and how you applied your approach to overcome it?
transcript.anchor_quote: I believe in leading from the front

transcript.text: The hardest thing as Senior Under Officer was that the 30 cadets were from very different years. Some of them arrived late for the 5:30 a.m. drill. I started a rule that late cadets did the opening drill, and the lateness stopped in a month.

You mentioned your final-year project was a low-cost solar water heater prototype reaching 55 degrees Celsius in four hours. Can you explain the key engineering principles you applied to achieve this performance?
Do you follow motorsport? I watched the last race with my friends, and I think the pit-stop strategy was the real story. It is quite similar to plant operations, in a way.
You drew a parallel between pit-stop strategies in motorsport and plant operations. Can you elaborate on how this comparison shapes your approach to managing manufacturing processes?
transcript.anchor_quote: I think the pit-stop strategy was the real story. It is quite similar to plant operations, in a way

transcript.text: I can't describe the plant's rejection rates or the customer names from my internship. They told us not to share production data outside the plant.
